newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA disciplines former Lehman Brothers trader.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA disciplines former Lehman Brothers trader.

text.p: UK financial markets regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Tuesday it had expelled a former Lehman Brothers senior trader for exceeding trading limits and attempting to disguise the true position.
It said the trader, Friedrich Kramer, had also been ordered to pay costs of 3,040 stg. It said he had admitted he failed to observe high standards of integrity and fair dealing.

The watchdog said that in November 1995, Kramer, then a senior trader at Lehman Brothers International (Europe) had agreed his management position limits relating to his trading in PIBOR futures contracts.
"Over the following three days Kramer exceeded both his intra-day and his overnight limits, the latter to a maximum of 35 times his agreed limit of 200 open contracts," the SFA said in a statement.
Lehman Brothers management questioned Kramer about exceeding his limits on his overnight position and was told he was within his trading limits.
The SFA added that Kramer had then unsuccessfully attempted to induce a trader at another firm to confirm fictitious trades in an attempt to disguise the true extent of the position.
Kramer then admitted his true position to management and was dismissed for the deception.

After his departure, Lehman Brothers reviewed the marks for all of the instruments in which Kramer dealt and found that between October 25 and November 21, he had been mismarking his French Treasury bill position and it had been overvalued by between $240,000 and $913,822.
